histoire.p1: Built in the 19<sup>th</sup> century, the Pensionnat de la Liberté had for decades taken in children who came to receive a strict education, far from their families.
histoire.p2: But one night in 1953, everything changed.
histoire.p3: Screams tore through the silence. Strange lights burst from the windows. Alerted, the police went to the scene… but what happened there was never revealed.
histoire.p4: The very next day, the boarding school was closed for good. The case was shelved. The events of that night were buried.
histoire.p5: Since then, the building has stood abandoned. And its secrets with it.
histoire.p6: Today, you have decided to reopen the case.
histoire.p7: Accompanied by our demonologist, you will step through the doors of the Pensionnat de la Liberté to find out what really happened that night.
histoire.conclusion: But some truths should perhaps have stayed buried.

meta.description: One passion, years of work and a forgotten boarding school: go behind the scenes of Memoria and discover the dark story of the Pensionnat de la Liberté.

hero.intro: Two stories cross paths here. One about enthusiasts who poured their energy into bringing Memoria to life. And one about the Pensionnat de la Liberté, whose doors should perhaps never have been reopened.

coulisses.intro: Memoria was born from a simple desire: to push the limits of immersion. Passionate about escape games, cinema and horror, we dreamed of an experience in which players would no longer be mere spectators, but the true protagonists of their own horror film.
coulisses.intro2: So, rather than wait for such an experience to exist, we decided to create it.
coulisses.role1: Founder · Script, staging and artistic direction
coulisses.bio1: A graduate of the Cours Florent drama school with a passion for theatre, cinema and immersive experiences, Sylvain brings the world of Memoria, its story and its characters to life. From writing the script to directing the actors, he shapes an experience in which every player becomes an actor in their own story.
coulisses.role2: Co-founder · Technical direction, design and development
coulisses.bio2: Passionate about games and immersive experiences, Alexis combines technical ingenuity, creativity and a strong sense of organisation, drawing on his experience in project management. From designing the sets to building the mechanisms, he turns ideas into real experiences. He brings his artistic sensibility and plays a key role in steering and developing Memoria.

genese.titre: From an idea to the first doors
genese.texte1: It all started around a table, after yet another escape game. One question kept coming back: what if you could live a real horror film, from the inside, face to face with real actors? The idea never left them.
genese.texte2: For months, the story was written, rewritten and tested. A boarding school, an unexplained closure in 1953, clues hidden in every room: every detail serves the story, every puzzle serves the fear.
genese.texte3: It had to be the right place. After dozens of visits, they found nearly 200 m² spread over three levels in Lyon: big enough to get lost in, intimate enough to feel watched.
genese.texte4: Hand-aged walls, second-hand furniture, antique objects and made-to-measure sets: every room was designed to make you feel that time stopped in 1953. Painstaking work, so that every corner tells a story.
genese.texte5: Spatial sound, controlled lighting, hidden mechanisms and real-time effects: the technology becomes invisible so you can only think about one thing… surviving.
genese.visuel5: The sound and light control room
genese.texte6: At the heart of Memoria are people. Actors trained in improvisation and controlled fear guide you, watch you and adjust the intensity to every group.

valeurs.texte3: Sets, props, mechanisms: almost everything was designed and built by us.

pensionnat.intro:
Of the Pensionnat de la Liberté, all that remains today are a few archives, yellowed photographs and the memory of a night in 1953 that no one seems willing to talk about.
Screams, strange lights, a police raid… then silence.
Here is what we have been able to piece together.
pensionnat.texte1:
Born into a prominent Lyon family, Alice de Saint-Symphorien sees her life turned upside down by the loss of her daughter, taken by tuberculosis.

Deeply marked by her grief, she decides to devote her fortune to founding an institution where every child, whatever their background, could find refuge, receive an education and grow up with respect and kindness.

And so the Pensionnat de la Liberté is born. Its motto, carved above its doors, will be handed down through the generations:

“Work uplifts, discipline straightens, obedience sets free.”
pensionnat.texte2:
A violent fire sweeps through the Pensionnat de la Liberté. The flames devour a large part of the building, taking with them precious archives and several decades of memories. Only a few damaged photographs survive the disaster.

The head supervisor dies in the fire, whose exact circumstances will never be established.

Determined to carry on her work, Alice de Saint-Symphorien orders the building to be rebuilt at once. The work allows the boarding school to reopen, but some basement rooms, too badly damaged, are sealed off for good.
pensionnat.titre3: In the shadow of the Great War
pensionnat.texte3:
The First World War hits the country hard, and the Pensionnat de la Liberté is not spared.

Despite shortages, restrictions and the departure of several staff members, the school carries on with its mission. New boarders find refuge there, sometimes separated from their families by the events shaking Europe.

Driven by Alice de Saint-Symphorien, the boarding school becomes, for many of these children, one of the few places where a semblance of normal life remains.
pensionnat.texte4:
After the ordeals of the war, the Pensionnat de la Liberté enjoys a period of prosperity. The number of boarders keeps growing, and the building has to be extended.

A new wing is built on the east side, making room for more children and improving their living conditions.

At the same time, major work is carried out in the basement, sealed off since the fire of 1904.

There, the workmen discover a room miraculously spared by the flames.

Refitted and opened to the boarders, it becomes a playroom, soon regarded as one of the children’s favourite places.
pensionnat.texte5:
As the Second World War plunges France into one of the darkest periods in its history, the Pensionnat de la Liberté quietly carries on.

True to its founder’s convictions, the school takes in and protects several children threatened by persecution, hiding their presence from the authorities.

The basement is refitted to serve as a shelter in case of danger. Old passages are reinforced, some rooms are converted and the windows blacked out.

Once places of life and play, these spaces gradually become cold, austere and oppressive, silent witnesses to a time when every sound could herald the worst.
pensionnat.legende5: The basement turned into a shelter
pensionnat.texte6:
After devoting nearly seventy years of her life to the Pensionnat de la Liberté, Alice de Saint-Symphorien passes away at a great age.

The running of the school is entrusted to Lucie Fiammetta, a trusted woman devoted to the values of kindness passed on by the founder.

Keen to preserve this legacy, the new headmistress has a warm office fitted out, full of books, keepsakes and familiar objects. She wants it to be a place of trust where every child can find a listening ear, comfort and protection.

Yet that same year, strange phenomena begin to be reported.

Noises echo through empty rooms. Some objects seem to move, and several boarders speak of events they struggle to explain.

The management tries to reassure the children, but the incidents multiply.
pensionnat.legende6: Lucie Fiammetta, headmistress of the school
pensionnat.texte7:
A new supervisor takes up his post at the Pensionnat de la Liberté.

As soon as he arrives, the man expresses the unusual wish to live inside the school itself. After some hesitation, the management agrees and has a room fitted out for him in the basement.

He quickly settles into his duties and helps look after the boarders every day.

At the time, unexplained events continue in the building. Some accounts mention noises at night coming from the lower levels.

No link will ever be officially established between these phenomena and the arrival of the new supervisor.
pensionnat.texte8:
On the night of 17 to 18 February 1953, the calm of the neighbourhood is brutally shattered.

Terrifying screams ring out inside the boarding school, while intense lights burst from several windows. Alerted by local residents, the police arrive quickly.

But when they get there, the building seems deserted.

No trace of the children. No trace of Lucie Fiammetta. No trace of the supervisor.

The officers enter the building to try to understand what has just happened.

The next day, the officers who took part in the operation are found in a state of deep madness, their eyes horribly mutilated. None of them will ever be able to give a coherent account of what happened that night.

Faced with the incomprehensible, the authorities decide to close the investigation. The reports are withheld from the public, the entrances sealed and the Pensionnat de la Liberté closed for good.

Since that night, none of its occupants has ever been found.
pensionnat.texte9:
In the midst of Lyon’s bustle, the Pensionnat de la Liberté still stands, almost invisible to those who walk past its walls.

A forgotten building, with dusty windows and closed doors, that seems to blend into the landscape.

Yet the people who live nearby sometimes tell strange stories.

A motionless figure glimpsed behind a window. A few notes of piano drifting from an abandoned room. Distant screams, muffled by the thickness of the walls.

Some even claim that lights still appear, on certain nights, in the windows of the boarding school.

No one knows what really happened on 18 February 1953.

And for more than seventy years, no one has dared to step through its doors again.

Until today.

experience.r1: Memoria is an immersive horror experience in Lyon. For 90 minutes, you and your group enter the Pensionnat de la Liberté, abandoned since 1953, and live a disturbing story from the inside, surrounded by professional actors and sets recreated down to the smallest detail.
experience.r2:
No, Memoria is not a traditional escape game, although it borrows some of its codes, such as searching, observing and working together.

It is above all an immersive experience in which the story, the interactions with the actors and the events unfolding around you take centre stage.

Here, you are not simply trying to solve puzzles or get out of a room: you are plunged into a terrifying investigation, in the corridors of the Pensionnat de la Liberté.
experience.q3: How long does the experience last?
experience.r3:
The immersive experience lasts 90 minutes. Please also allow an extra 15 minutes afterwards for the debriefing and your departure.

So plan on spending about 1 hour 45 minutes on site.
experience.q4: How many players can take part?
experience.r4:
Each session usually welcomes 3 to 6 players.

For special events, birthdays, hen and stag parties or team building, we can exceptionally welcome up to 8 players in the same session.

These special requests must be made through our contact form so that our team can organise your visit.

For larger groups, several sessions can also be arranged. Discover our Team building and Tailor-made experience offers.
experience.r5: Yes. Professional actors play the characters of the boarding school. They interact with you, guide you… or put you to the test, and adapt their performance to each group.
experience.q6: Do I need to be fit?
experience.r6: No, no particular level of fitness is required. You will walk, go up and down stairs (the boarding school spreads over three levels) and sometimes crouch, but never run or make any intense effort.
experience.r7:
Not really! Unlike a traditional escape game, Memoria is not mainly about solving puzzles.

You will mostly search, look for objects, carry out certain actions and react to the events unfolding around you.

A few moments of thinking and deduction will still be needed. After all, you are taking part in a most perilous investigation… and every discovery could matter.
experience.r8: Most of the time, yes. Depending on the story and the intensity level chosen, some passages may separate the group for a few moments, always under the watch of our team.
experience.r9:
Yes, at any time and with no obligation to carry on. Your safety and your consent always come first.

A safety signal will be explained to you at the start of the experience. If the experience becomes too intense, simply use it to stop your participation immediately.

A member of our team will then come and take you out of the experience.
experience.q10: Can we take part with only two players?
experience.r10:
Memoria is designed for a minimum of 3 players per session.

It is nevertheless possible to take part with only two people, on prior request to our team.

In that case, the session is charged at the 3-player rate.

Contact us through our form to arrange your visit.

intensite.q1: What are the three intensity levels?
intensite.r1:
Day Boarder: a disturbing atmosphere, surprises and controlled tension. Ideal for discovering the world of Memoria with no physical contact with the actors.

Boarder: the balance between tension, chills and interaction with the actors. The experience as we imagined it, with some possible physical contact and more intense immersion.

Straight to Hell!: at your own risk. An experience pushed to its maximum intensity, with more interaction, supervised physical contact and gruelling situations. For those who want to push their limits.
intensite.r2:
Yes, depending on the intensity level chosen.

At the Day Boarder level, no physical contact with the actors is planned.

At the Boarder and Straight to Hell! levels, physical contact may occur as part of the experience.

However, no rough handling, inappropriate gestures or dangerous behaviour are ever tolerated.

You can refuse physical contact by saying so at the start of the experience. Our actors adapt their interactions accordingly.
intensite.r3:
The intensity level is chosen when booking. By default, the Boarder level is selected.

You can still change your choice when you arrive, before the session starts.

During the experience, our actors keep a close eye on how participants react and can adjust the intensity if a player is struggling.
intensite.q4: Is the “Straight to Hell!” level compulsory?
intensite.r4: Not at all. The Boarder level is the one we recommend to most groups. The Straight to Hell! level is an option for those who want a particularly intense experience.
intensite.q5: Is the experience suitable for sensitive people?
intensite.r5: Yes, thanks to the Day Boarder level, designed to let you live the story with a shiver without being overwhelmed. If in doubt, contact us before booking: we will help you choose the level best suited to your group.
intensite.q6: What happens if a player is too scared?
intensite.r6:
They can ask for a break or leave the experience at any time using the safety signal explained at the start of the experience.

A member of our team then steps in to take them to a quiet space, while the rest of the group carries on with the adventure.

No one is ever forced to continue.

As our sessions follow a precise schedule, any delay may shorten your experience, with no change to the price.

If you are more than 25 minutes late, the session may be cancelled and not take place.

We therefore recommend allowing plenty of time to reach us.
reservation.r6:
Yes! With our split payment system, each participant can pay their own share of the booking.

If you have any difficulty or need help organising your payment, do not hesitate to contact our team.
reservation.q7: Can I use a gift voucher?
reservation.r7: Yes. Enter your voucher code when booking online: it is applied automatically. Vouchers are valid for 12 months. Want to give one? Head to the Give Memoria page.
reservation.q8: Can we hire the venue privately?
reservation.r8: Yes, for a birthday, a corporate event or a special occasion: several time slots or the whole venue can be reserved for you. Discover our tailor-made pack and our team building offers.

pratique.r1: The experience is not allowed for under-12s and not recommended for under-16s. Minors must be accompanied by an adult taking part in the session.
pratique.r2: Comfortable clothes and flat, closed shoes. Avoid delicate or light-coloured clothing: the boarding school was abandoned for a long time… Your personal belongings can be left at the welcome desk.
pratique.r3: At 45 cours de la Liberté, Lyon. Find the map and our contact details in the practical information.
pratique.r4:
Memoria is easy to reach by public transport and Vélo’v bike.

  • Metro D: Guillotière
  • Metro B: Place Guichard
  • Tram T1: Liberté
  • Bus C9: Liberté
  • Vélo’v: 32 cours de la Liberté

We recommend using public transport to get here.
pratique.r5: There are several public car parks nearby. We still recommend public transport, which is more convenient in the city centre.
pratique.q6: Is the venue accessible to people with disabilities?
pratique.r6:
The Pensionnat de la Liberté is spread over several levels, some of which can only be reached by stairs. The full route is therefore not accessible to people with reduced mobility.

However, we want everyone to be able to live the Memoria experience. That is why we offer a personalised, adapted version that lets people with reduced mobility take full part in the adventure, depending on their needs and what can be arranged.

We also have toilets accessible to people with reduced mobility.

For any specific request, please contact us before booking, so that we can prepare your visit in the best possible conditions.
pratique.r7: The experience includes sudden sound and light effects, passages in the dark and confined spaces. It is not recommended for people with heart conditions, epilepsy, severe anxiety or claustrophobia, or for pregnant women. Anyone under the influence of alcohol or drugs will be refused entry.
pratique.q8: Can I come if I am pregnant?
pratique.r8: As a precaution, the experience is not recommended for pregnant women, because of the strong emotions, sudden effects and moving around in the dark. The other members of your group are of course welcome to take part.
pratique.q9: Can I take part with a heart or medical condition?
pratique.r9: People with heart conditions or health problems that could be worsened by intense stress must not take part. If in doubt, ask your doctor for advice and talk to us before booking.

s3.contenu:
MEMORIA offers an immersive horror experience combining live theatre, interactive storytelling, sets, technical effects and actors.

Participants are plunged into a fiction set in the Pensionnat de la Liberté, a fictional boarding school abandoned since 1953.

The experience is not a traditional escape game.

It relies mainly on immersion, interaction, exploration, observation and the players’ active participation in a scripted investigation.

Actions, searches and moments of reflection may be needed for the adventure to unfold.

The usual length of the experience is 90 minutes.

The customer should also allow:

  • About 15 minutes after the session for the debriefing and departure.

The total recommended time on the premises is therefore about 1 hour 45 minutes.

The 90 minutes correspond to the planned length of the immersive route. This length may be affected by the group arriving late, an interruption requested by a participant or a safety requirement.

MEMORIA undertakes to provide a service that complies with the characteristics announced and the applicable contractual conditions.

The subjective perception of fear, of the emotions felt or of how difficult the events are does not in itself constitute a lack of conformity of the service.

s4.contenu:
4.1. Standard sessions

Each session usually welcomes between 3 and 6 players.

The number of participants is set when booking.

4.2. Taking part with two players

A session may exceptionally be arranged for two people, subject to a prior request and MEMORIA’s agreement.

In that case, the price charged is that of a three-player session.

4.3. Groups of 7 or 8 players

For special events, birthdays, hen and stag parties and team building services, MEMORIA may exceptionally welcome up to 8 players in the same session.

These bookings cannot be made automatically in the standard calendar.

They require a prior request through the contact form and MEMORIA’s express confirmation.

The price and specific conditions are communicated before the order is confirmed.

4.4. Groups of more than eight people

Groups of more than eight participants can benefit from a specific organisation, in particular by spreading the players over several sessions.

The schedule, times, capacities and prices are set in advance in a quote.

4.5. Absence of a participant

A booking is for a set number of places.

If one or more participants do not attend, the places booked remain payable, unless a change has been accepted under the conditions of Article 12 or the law provides otherwise.

A change in the number of participants does not automatically entitle the customer to a recalculation of the price or a refund of unused places.

s6.contenu:
Standard bookings are mainly made online via the website www.memoria-experience.fr, using the 4escape solution.

The customer selects in particular:

  • The session time.
  • The number of players.
  • The intensity level.
  • Any additional services offered.

Before final confirmation, the customer must be able to check the order summary, the total price and the information needed to carry out the order.

The customer must be able to correct any errors before confirming the purchase.

Confirming the order must clearly indicate that it entails an obligation to pay.

The booking becomes firm once the payment due has been validated, subject to the confirmation sent by MEMORIA or its booking system.

A summary email is sent to the address provided by the customer.

It sets out in particular the essential information about the booking.

The customer is responsible for the accuracy of the contact details provided.

If no confirmation is received or a payment issue occurs, the customer is asked to contact MEMORIA before placing a new order.

The booking is for the session, date and time shown in the confirmation.

Any later change is subject to the conditions set out in these Terms.

s7.contenu:
Online bookings are paid using the 4escape solution and its associated payment systems.

The payment methods actually accepted are shown to the customer before the order is confirmed.

For standard sessions, full payment is required when booking, unless a specific arrangement is expressly offered.

Split payment

Where this feature is offered by the booking system, participants can split the payment.

Each player can then pay their share according to the terms communicated by the platform.

The booking is only finally confirmed once the required payment conditions have been met.

The precise terms for splitting payments, any deadlines and how incomplete payments are handled are those shown before the order is confirmed.

In case of difficulty, the customer can contact MEMORIA at contact@memoria-experience.fr.

For business or tailor-made services, payment deadlines are set in the accepted quote.

s8.contenu:
MEMORIA offers three intensity levels so that the interactions and fear effects can be adapted to the group’s sensitivity.

8.1. Day Boarder (Demi-pensionnaire)

This level focuses on a disturbing atmosphere, psychological tension and measured interaction.

No deliberate physical contact between actors and players is planned as part of the staging.

8.2. Boarder (Pensionnaire)

This level corresponds to the standard experience recommended by MEMORIA.

It offers more intense immersion, with tense situations, surprises and stronger interaction.

Non-violent physical contact may occur as part of the staging, with respect for the participants’ consent.

8.3. Straight to Hell! (Jusqu’en enfer !)

This level corresponds to the maximum intensity offered by MEMORIA.

It includes more sustained fear situations, more direct interaction and supervised physical contact.

No intensity level permits rough handling, violence, humiliation, inappropriate gestures or dangerous behaviour.

8.4. Choosing the level

The intensity level is selected when booking.

By default, the Boarder level is offered.

The choice can be changed before the session starts, subject to organisational and safety conditions.

During the experience, the actors may adapt their interactions if a participant’s condition or reactions require it.

Choosing an intensity level never amounts to a waiver of participants’ fundamental rights or to general consent to any physical contact.

s9.contenu:
The MEMORIA experience is not permitted for people under 12.

It is not recommended for minors under 16 because of its horror nature and the emotional intensity of some sequences.

Any minor participant must be accompanied by an adult who actually takes part in the session.

Where the accompanying adult does not hold parental authority, they must have the necessary authorisation for the minor to take part.

MEMORIA may ask for appropriate proof where necessary to check that these conditions are met.

The accompanying adult must ensure that the minors in their care follow the instructions, without prejudice to MEMORIA’s safety obligations.

The intensity level must be suited to the participants’ age and sensitivity.

MEMORIA may refuse an intensity level that is clearly unsuitable for a participant, on objective safety grounds.

s10.titre: Article 10 — Health, warnings and physical conditions
s10.contenu:
The experience includes in particular:

  • Sometimes sudden or intense sound effects.
  • Significant variations in lighting.
  • Passages in semi-darkness.
  • Visual and lighting effects that may be startling.
  • Situations of fear and psychological tension.
  • Moving around in fitted-out spaces.
  • Stairs and some confined spaces.
  • Close interaction with actors.

Participation is not recommended for people who are particularly sensitive to strong emotions, certain light or sound effects, confined spaces or intense stress.

Particular caution is recommended for people with heart conditions, photosensitivity (in particular linked to certain forms of epilepsy) or health problems that may be aggravated by the experience.

As a precaution, MEMORIA also advises pregnant women not to take part.

If in doubt about their fitness to take part, the people concerned are invited to seek medical advice before booking.

No particular physical fitness is required for the standard route.

However, it may be necessary to walk, bend down or use stairs.

Players are never asked to run.

The customer is asked to inform the other participants of the main characteristics and warnings of the experience before the session.

Any request for adjustments must be sent to MEMORIA before booking.

Participants are not asked to give MEMORIA a detailed medical diagnosis. Only the information strictly necessary to consider an adjustment or for safety should be requested, in compliance with the regulations on personal data.

s11.contenu:
11.1. Safety instructions

Safety instructions are given to participants at the start of each session.

They cover in particular:

  • The characteristics of the route and its main risks.
  • The rules for moving around the building.
  • The ban on running.
  • Precautions regarding the stairs, sets and technical installations.
  • The rules applying to interaction with the actors.
  • The limits of physical contact.
  • How to stop the experience voluntarily.
  • The safety signal for calling the team.
  • The instructions in the event of an incident or evacuation.

These instructions are adapted to the characteristics of the experience, the intensity level chosen and, where necessary, the audience concerned.

The main safety rules are also displayed in writing on the premises.

Each participant must follow the instructions given.

A certificate of acknowledgement of the instructions may be collected individually before the session starts.

This certificate does not constitute a waiver of liability in favour of MEMORIA.

11.2. Safety signal

A safety signal is given to the players at the start of the experience.

This signal allows any participant to ask to stop taking part when the experience becomes too intense or when they wish to stop.

Using it brings the team to intervene as quickly as safety allows.

The person concerned is taken to a suitable area.

11.3. Freedom to stop the experience

No participant is obliged to continue the experience against their will.

They may ask to leave at any time.

One participant stopping does not necessarily end the session for the other players.

Where a participant leaves of their own accord, through no fault of MEMORIA, this does not automatically give rise to a refund, subject to the applicable legal provisions.

11.4. Physical contact

Physical contact is strictly supervised.

It may be offered at the Boarder and Straight to Hell! levels, but must always remain compatible with the participants’ safety, dignity and consent.

Any player may refuse physical contact by saying so at the start of or during the experience.

The actors must respect this refusal.

11.5. Interruption for safety reasons

MEMORIA may temporarily interrupt a sequence, adapt the route or end a session if a situation poses a serious risk to participants or staff.

Where this situation results from a participant’s behaviour, the provisions of Article 23 apply.

The contractual consequences of an interruption not attributable to the participants are assessed in accordance with the customer’s legal rights.

s12.contenu:
A request to change a booking can be made up to 48 hours before the scheduled session time.

Changes remain subject to slot availability and MEMORIA’s agreement.

The request must be sent to:

contact@memoria-experience.fr

It must state the booking number and the change requested.

A change only takes effect once MEMORIA has confirmed it in writing.

If no new slot can be agreed, the original booking remains in force, unless otherwise agreed or a legal right to terminate applies.

After the 48-hour deadline, a change request may be considered on an exceptional basis, with no guarantee that it will be accepted.

Accepted changes may lead to a price adjustment where they alter the characteristics of the service. This adjustment must be communicated and accepted before confirmation.

s13.contenu:
13.1. Requests made at least 72 hours before the session

A cancellation request can be made at least 72 hours before the scheduled session time, for a legitimate and justified reason.

The following may in particular be considered legitimate reasons:

  • An illness or accident actually preventing participation.
  • A death or serious family event.
  • An exceptional, unforeseeable circumstance beyond the customer’s control making participation impossible.
  • An objectively established inability to travel, in exceptional circumstances.

This list is not exhaustive.

The request must be accompanied by proportionate supporting documents strictly necessary to assess its merits.

MEMORIA does not require detailed medical information where less intrusive documents can establish the impediment.

Where a cancellation is accepted under these conditions, MEMORIA refunds in full the sums paid for the booking concerned.

The commercial refund is made within a maximum of 14 days of the written acceptance of the cancellation, unless otherwise agreed with the customer.

13.2. Requests made less than 72 hours before the session

A cancellation requested less than 72 hours before the session starts does not automatically give rise to a refund.

MEMORIA may nevertheless consider exceptional circumstances put forward by the customer and offer an amicable solution, in particular a postponement.

A postponement may be considered, on presentation of appropriate proof, where a serious or unforeseeable event prevents participation.

Acceptance of a postponement remains subject to MEMORIA’s organisational possibilities, without prejudice to the customer’s legal rights.

13.3. Cancellation without an admissible reason

Where the customer gives up their booking without a reason meeting the accepted cancellation conditions, no commercial refund is guaranteed.

This rule does not deprive the customer of any rights they may have under the applicable law.

13.4. Absence on the day of the session

If the group does not attend without a cancellation having been accepted beforehand, the service booked remains payable, subject to the applicable legal provisions.

Any cancellation request must be sent to:

contact@memoria-experience.fr

s14.contenu:
Participants must arrive 5 minutes before the scheduled start of their session.

This allows the session to start on time.

If running late, participants must inform MEMORIA as soon as possible.

As sessions follow precise time slots, a delay attributable to the participants may shorten their experience.

If the group is more than 25 minutes late compared with the scheduled start of the session, MEMORIA may refuse to start the experience.

This decision takes into account in particular organisational constraints, the following bookings and safety conditions.

Where the session cannot take place because of a delay attributable to the customer, no commercial refund is guaranteed, subject to mandatory legal provisions.

MEMORIA may offer an exceptional postponement where circumstances allow.

Lateness is measured against the session start time shown in the confirmation, not the recommended arrival time.

s15.titre: Article 15 — Cancellation or change by MEMORIA
s15.contenu:
MEMORIA may have to cancel or postpone a session when it cannot be carried out under the agreed conditions.

This may result in particular from:

  • A technical incident preventing normal operation of the route.
  • A safety problem.
  • The unforeseen unavailability of an actor essential to the service.
  • An administrative closure.
  • A force majeure event.
  • Any other circumstance actually preventing the planned service from being performed.

MEMORIA informs the customer as soon as it becomes aware that the session cannot take place.

Where the service cannot be performed, the customer may accept a postponement to another date.

Failing agreement on a postponement, and where the contract is terminated in accordance with the applicable provisions, the sums paid for the service not performed are refunded within the legal time limits.

Cancellation or change attributable to MEMORIA does not deprive the customer of their other legal rights, in particular where the conditions for compensation are met.

A substantial change to the service cannot be imposed unilaterally on the customer outside the cases permitted by law.

s16.contenu:
16.1. Bookings for a specific date

In accordance with Article L.221-28, 12° of the French Consumer Code, the right of withdrawal does not apply to contracts for leisure activities to be provided on a specific date or during a specific period.

Consequently, bookings of MEMORIA sessions for a specific date do not benefit from the 14-day legal withdrawal period.

The options for changing and commercially cancelling a booking are those set out in these Terms.

16.2. Purchase of gift vouchers without a set session date

The distance purchase of a gift voucher without a simultaneous booking of a service on a specific date may be covered by the legal right of withdrawal.

Where applicable, the consumer customer has 14 days from the conclusion of the contract to exercise this right, without having to give a reason.

Withdrawal can be exercised using the form in the appendix, an unambiguous statement or the online withdrawal feature made available in accordance with the regulations.

The refund is made according to the terms and time limits set by the French Consumer Code.

Where a voucher has been used or a service has begun during the withdrawal period, the consequences are assessed in light of the applicable legal provisions and the information given to the consumer before ordering.

16.3. Additional digital content

Where MEMORIA sells a video or other digital content separately, the rules on the right of withdrawal depend on the nature of the service, its personalisation and the conditions under which its supply begins.

Any exception to or loss of this right must meet the applicable legal conditions and be subject to the information and, where necessary, the express agreements required.

s17.contenu:
17.1. Nature of gift vouchers

MEMORIA offers gift vouchers for giving an immersive experience.

These vouchers correspond to a package for a set number of players.

17.2. Validity

Gift vouchers are valid for 12 months from their date of purchase.

The expiry date is shown on the voucher or in the confirmation email.

The precise conditions for booking before the voucher expires must be communicated to the recipient.

17.3. Use

The recipient makes a booking according to the availability offered by MEMORIA.

They must enter the gift voucher code when booking or follow the procedure communicated when it was issued.

A gift voucher does not guarantee the availability of a particular slot.

The recipient is therefore invited to book well in advance.

17.4. Price difference

s22.titre: Article 22 — Accessibility and adaptation of the route
s22.contenu:
The Pensionnat de la Liberté is spread over several levels, some of which are connected by stairs.

The full standard route is not accessible to people with reduced mobility.

MEMORIA is nevertheless willing to consider personalised adaptations so that the people concerned can enjoy an immersive experience compatible with their needs and with safety conditions.

The venue has toilets adapted for people with reduced mobility.

Any request for adaptation must be sent to MEMORIA before booking, through the contact form or by email.

After discussing it with the customer, MEMORIA specifies the adjustments actually possible and the characteristics of the route offered.

An adaptation is confirmed in writing before the corresponding booking is concluded.

No service or area that is not actually accessible may be presented as accessible.

s23.titre: Article 23 — Rules of conduct, exclusion and ending a session
s23.contenu:
Participants undertake to respect the safety rules, the actors, the staff, the other players, the premises and the equipment.

The following are prohibited in particular:

  • Physical violence and threats.
  • Insults, intimidation and discriminatory or harassing behaviour.
  • Non-consensual physical contact with staff or other participants.
  • Deliberate damage to sets and props.
  • Unauthorised handling of technical installations.
  • Bringing in dangerous objects.
  • Any behaviour likely to endanger others.

23.1. Alcohol and drugs

It is forbidden to bring in or consume alcohol, drugs or any other psychoactive substance for unauthorised use on the premises.

An exception may be made for alcoholic drinks served by MEMORIA or its caterer as part of a Cocktail service, exclusively after the end of the immersive experience, under the conditions applicable to that service.

Participants must follow the consumption and safety rules communicated by the venue.

No participant showing clear signs of intoxication or impairment by a psychoactive substance may take part in the experience where their condition is incompatible with it being carried out safely.

23.2. Refusal of access to the experience

MEMORIA may refuse access to anyone who:

  • Shows clear signs of intoxication or of being under the influence of drugs or other psychoactive substances incompatible with taking part safely.
  • Behaves violently, threateningly or in a seriously insulting manner towards other participants or staff.
  • Refuses to follow the essential safety instructions after they have been clearly explained.

The decision to refuse access is based on objective grounds, assessed in light of the facts observed and the safety requirements of the activity.

23.3. Exclusion and ending the session

The session manager may at any time exclude one or more participants or, if safety requires, end the session for the whole group where a participant:

  • Commits violence, makes threats or imposes non-consensual physical contact on an actor, a member of staff or another player.
  • Is clearly under the influence of alcohol or drugs, in a way incompatible with the safety of the experience.
  • Deliberately damages the sets, props or technical installations.
  • Persists in breaching the essential safety instructions despite a warning from the team.
  • Seriously endangers their own safety or that of others.

Except in the event of violence, a serious threat or immediate danger, a warning is given before exclusion.

Where only one participant’s behaviour is at issue, MEMORIA favours excluding that person and continuing the session for the other players, where safety and organisational conditions allow.

If a participant’s behaviour makes it impossible to continue the session safely for the whole group, the manager may decide to stop the experience for good.

MEMORIA may call the police if the situation warrants it.

23.4. Financial consequences

Where a refusal of access, exclusion or interruption is directly attributable to a participant’s serious breach of these rules, that participant is not automatically entitled to a refund or postponement.

In the absence of any breach attributable to MEMORIA, no commercial refund is guaranteed to the participant responsible, subject to the applicable legal provisions.

Where a whole session is stopped because of the behaviour of a single participant, the financial consequences are examined by distinguishing the situation of the participant responsible from that of the other players.

Participants who have committed no breach retain their legal rights relating to the service not performed.

A postponement, a refund corresponding to the service not performed or another amicable solution may be offered to them depending on the circumstances and the applicable obligations.

Material damage or bodily injury caused by a participant may give rise to their personal liability under the conditions provided for by law.

These provisions do not affect customers’ rights in the event of MEMORIA failing to meet its own obligations.

s24.titre: Article 24 — Liability and compliance with safety instructions
s24.contenu:
MEMORIA is required to perform the services in accordance with the contract and its legal obligations.

It takes the measures necessary for the safety of participants and the smooth running of the activities offered.

24.1. Safety instructions

The safety instructions necessary for the activity are presented to each participant at the start of the experience.

They are adapted to the characteristics of the route, the audience concerned and the reasonably foreseeable risks.

The essential instructions are also displayed in writing on the premises.

Each participant undertakes to follow these instructions and the directions given by the team throughout their time on the premises.

A participant who breaches the safety instructions or behaves wrongfully may be held liable for the damage they cause to other participants, staff or installations.

Where their fault has contributed to their own damage, this may result in MEMORIA being fully or partly exempted from liability, only under the conditions provided for by law.

This liability is assessed taking into account in particular MEMORIA’s safety, information and prevention obligations.

24.2. Material damage

Participants must respect the installations and equipment made available to them.

Damage caused intentionally or through fault may give rise to the liability of its author under ordinary law.

MEMORIA may claim compensation for material damage actually suffered, provided it can prove its reality and amount.

24.3. Personal belongings

Participants are advised not to bring valuables.

Any arrangements for leaving personal belongings are explained by the team on site.

MEMORIA’s liability in the event of loss, theft or damage is assessed in accordance with the applicable legal rules and the circumstances.

24.4. Legal limits

No provision of these Terms may have the effect of excluding or limiting a liability that the law prohibits from being excluded or limited.

These Terms do not constitute a waiver of liability regarding the safety of persons.

Taking part in the experience and accepting these conditions do not entail any advance waiver of a legally recognised right to compensation.

s25.contenu:
Force majeure situations are assessed in accordance with Article 1218 of the French Civil Code.

Where an event meeting the legal conditions of force majeure temporarily prevents the performance of a contractual obligation, the consequences are determined in accordance with the applicable legal provisions.

Where the impediment is permanent, the contract may be terminated under the conditions provided for by law, with the corresponding restitution.

A technical, organisational or financial difficulty does not automatically constitute force majeure.

The party invoking a force majeure event informs the other party as quickly as reasonably possible.
